module.purpose: Provides versioned NestJS HTTP endpoints for platform booking creation, retrieval, cancellation, rescheduling, recurring bookings, instant meetings, and no-show handling.
module.summary: This controller adapts API v2 booking requests into platform-library operations. It authenticates API and OAuth callers, resolves platform configuration and ownership, normalizes request bodies, delegates booking workflows, translates domain errors into HTTP exceptions, and records billing usage for created or cancelled bookings.
module.businessContext: Serves Cal.com platform integrations managing customer bookings and scheduling workflows. Failure prevents external clients from creating, retrieving, cancelling, or reconciling bookings and usage.

invariants.description: Successful endpoint responses use SUCCESS_STATUS and place results under data.
Booking creation requests are marked with API_V2 as their creation source.
Platform email settings determine whether normalized requests set noEmail.
Cancellation billing usage is adjusted only after the cancellation handler returns.
Recurring booking entries without an identifier receive one shared generated identifier.

assumptions.description: Callers provide booking input shapes compatible with the platform-library handlers.
Cancellation callers provide a public booking UID rather than a numeric database ID.
Booking responses expose userId, uid, startTime, and related billing fields expected by usage services.
API key prefix configuration is available through ConfigService when API-key ownership is resolved.
NestJS dependency injection supplies repositories, services, and guards before endpoint invocation.

ambiguities.question: Whether billing usage updates must complete before the HTTP response is considered durable.
Whether the recurring booking handler safely accepts an empty request array.
Whether the two request-normalization helpers are intentionally divergent in where noEmail and creationSource are assigned.

concurrencyModel.notes: Endpoints await primary booking operations, while billing usage updates are deliberately launched without waiting for completion; recurring usage updates use forEach with async callbacks.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A user requests bookings without a status filter.
given: queryParams = { filters: undefined, cursor: undefined, limit: undefined }
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins default status, pagination defaults, and next-cursor behavior.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A cancellation request uses a numeric booking identifier instead of a UID.
moduleContractTests.then: the call throws BadRequestException with message "Please provide booking uid instead of booking id."
moduleContractTests.rationale: Prevents accidental cancellation by numeric booking ID.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A cancellation request targets an existing booking that is already cancelled.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Enforces idempotency protection for already-cancelled bookings.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A booking lookup or reschedule lookup returns no booking.
moduleContractTests.then: the call throws NotFoundException with message `Booking with UID=${bookingUid} does not exist.`
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins the public not-found response for unknown booking UIDs.
